Shared context from the other agents working on this task (session sales-pipeline, up to stream sequence 32).
The task: Build a nightly pipeline that loads sales exports and produces a weekly revenue report. master-a owns ingestion, master-b owns the report.

Each entry names the agent that reported it. Treat entries as that agent's results and decisions, not your own conclusions, and check anything critical before relying on it. Declared entries were shared deliberately by their agent; the others were picked out of its work. Entries marked as conflicting disagree and are unresolved.

## ingestion
- [decision from master-a, seq 7, #29] Update: DuckDB can't be written by two processes at once, which breaks the backfill plan. We're switching to Postgres for the warehouse.
- [fact from master-a, seq 1, #20] The exports arrive as CSV in an S3 bucket, one file per store per day. I checked last month's files: 312 files, the largest is 48 MB.

## report
- [artifact from master-b, seq 7, #37] Draft metric definition:
  ```sql
  SELECT date_trunc('week', ts) AS week,
         sum(CASE WHEN type = 'REFUND' THEN -amount ELSE amount END) AS net_revenue
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY 1;
  ```
- [fact from master-b, seq 5, #31] The report will be generated as a PDF and emailed to finance every Monday at 07:00.

## scheduling
- [fact from master-a, seq 8, #32] The pipeline runs nightly at 02:00 UTC from a cron job on the ops box.

## data
- [fact from master-a, seq 6, #27] All timestamps in the exports are UTC. Week boundaries will be Monday 00:00 UTC; that's settled.
- [fact from master-a, seq 4, #24] Refunds are separate rows with type=REFUND and a positive amount, so the report has to subtract them.
- [fact from master-a, seq 3, #23] Tool call read_file({"path": "exports/README.txt"}) returned:
  Refunds are exported as separate rows with type=REFUND and a positive amount.

## data_quality
- [decision from master-a, seq 9, #34] 0.4% of rows have an empty store_id; we drop them and log a count.
- [fact from master-a, seq 9, #35] Duplicate order IDs appear when a store re-exports a day; we keep the latest file.

## Open questions
Unresolved; answer them if you can, and do not treat them as settled.
- [open question from master-a, seq 9, #36, topic data] How should we treat orders with a negative quantity?
- [open question from master-a, seq 1, #21, topic ingestion] I'm not sure yet whether refunds show up as negative rows or in a separate file.

Shared context from the other agents working on this task (session url-shortener, up to stream sequence 699).
The task: Build a URL shortener HTTP API. master-a owns storage and IDs, master-b owns the HTTP API.

Each entry names the agent that reported it. Treat entries as that agent's results and decisions, not your own conclusions, and check anything critical before relying on it. Declared entries were shared deliberately by their agent; the others were picked out of its work. Entries marked as conflicting disagree and are unresolved.

Agents may disagree on: storage (master-a, master-b). Resolve these first.

## storage (decisions from master-a and master-b; check that they agree)
- [decision from master-a, seq 6, #681] Change of plan after talking it through: for the MVP we'll use SQLite instead of Postgres. One file, no server to run, and our expected load is small. Postgres stays an option for later.
- [decision from master-b, seq 7, #682] I decided to keep the link table in Redis for now, it was quicker to wire up in the API service.

## http_api
- [fact from master-b, seq 10, #690] All 18 API tests pass.
- [fact from master-b, seq 5, #679] Tool call lookup({"query": "which HTTP status for a URL shortener redirect"}) returned:
  Use 302 Found for links that may change; 301 is cached permanently by browsers.
- [fact from master-b, seq 10, #688] POST /links validates URLs and rejects anything that isn't http or https.
- [decision from master-b, seq 6, #680] We will return 302 for redirects, not 301, so links can be edited later.
- [artifact from master-b, seq 9, #687] Here is the redirect handler:
  ```python
  @app.get("/{code}")
  async def redirect(code: str):
      if len(code) > 7:
          raise HTTPException(404)
      url = await store.resolve(code)
      if url is None:
          raise HTTPException(404)
      return RedirectResponse(url, status_code=302)
  ```
- [fact from master-b, seq 1, #674] Taking the HTTP API: POST /links to create, GET /{code} to redirect.
- [fact from master-b, seq 10, #689] GET /{code} returns 404 for unknown codes.

## ids
- [decision from master-a, seq 1, #668] I'll take the storage layer and ID generation.
- [fact from master-a, seq 5, #677] Short codes are the bigint ID encoded in base62, left-padded to 7 characters. That's final; max length is 7.

## testing
- [fact from master-a, seq 9, #685] Load test on SQLite with WAL enabled: 1,200 creates/s and 9,000 redirects/s, p99 latency 45 ms. That's well above what we need.

## Open questions
Unresolved; answer them if you can, and do not treat them as settled.
- [open question from master-a, seq 3, #673, topic analytics] Open question for whoever owns the API: do we need per-link click analytics in the MVP? It changes the schema a lot.
- [open question from master-b, seq 11, #694, topic rate_limiting] Still unsure whether we need rate limiting on POST /links.
